requirements.original: There are two possible notations: either a simple string when the variant is related to a single encode attribute or a comma separated list of strings enclosed in curly brackets if the variant is related to multiple encodings.
requirements.canonical: When the variant is related to multiple encodings, the first part of an encoding related variant attribute IS a comma separated list of strings enclosed in curly brackets.
requirements.condition: variant related to multiple encodings
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.5 -- There are two possible notations: either a simple string when the variant is related to a single encode attribute or a comma separated list of strings enclosed in curly brackets if the variant is related to multiple encodings.

requirements.original: The second part of the attribute (following the dot symbol) is a simple string that specifies the variant value.
requirements.canonical: The second part (following the dot) of an encoding related variant attribute IS a simple string that specifies the variant value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.5 -- The second part of the attribute (following the dot symbol) is a simple string that specifies the variant value.

requirements.original: The encoding related attributes are valid only when the related encoding is selected.
requirements.canonical: An encoding related variant attribute IS valid only when the related encoding is selected.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.5 -- The encoding related attributes are valid only when the related encoding is selected.

requirements.original: It is not allowed to define variant attributes with no encoding reference if multiple encodings are used.
requirements.canonical: If multiple encodings are used, a variant attribute SHALL NOT be defined without an encoding reference.
requirements.condition: multiple encodings are used
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.5 -- It is not allowed to define variant attributes with no encoding reference if multiple encodings are used.

requirements.original: The with statement can contain any number of variant attributes.
requirements.canonical: A with statement MAY contain any number of variant attributes.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.5 -- The with statement can contain any number of variant attributes.

requirements.original: a) When dot notation is used in the variant attribute value for an element, the strings preceding the dot symbol shall resolve into one of the encode attribute values associated with the same element.
requirements.canonical: When dot notation is used in the variant attribute value for an element, the strings preceding the dot SHALL resolve into one of the encode attribute values associated with the same element.
requirements.condition: dot notation is used in the variant attribute value
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.5 -- a) When dot notation is used in the variant attribute value for an element, the strings preceding the dot symbol shall resolve into one of the encode attribute values associated with the same element.

requirements.original: The with statement may contain any number of extension attributes.
requirements.canonical: A with statement MAY contain any number of extension attributes.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.6 -- The with statement may contain any number of extension attributes.

requirements.original: extension
requirements.canonical: An extension attribute IS denoted by the keyword `extension` in a with statement.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.6 -- extension

requirements.original: All TTCN-3 language elements can have extension attributes specified by the user.
requirements.canonical: An extension attribute MAY be specified by the user for any TTCN-3 language element.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.6 -- All TTCN-3 language elements can have extension attributes specified by the user.

requirements.original: optional
requirements.canonical: An optional attribute IS denoted by the keyword `optional` in a with statement.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.7 -- optional

requirements.original: TTCN-3 constants, module parameters, templates, variables and template variables can have an optional attribute.
requirements.canonical: An optional attribute MAY be associated with a constant, module parameter, template, variable or template variable.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.7 -- TTCN-3 constants, module parameters, templates, variables and template variables can have an optional attribute.

requirements.original: Also, TTCN-3 language elements that contain such definitions, i.e. module, group, function, altstep, test case, control, and component type definitions can have an optional attribute.
requirements.canonical: An optional attribute MAY be associated with a module, group, function, altstep, testcase, module control function or component type definition.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.7 -- Also, TTCN-3 language elements that contain such definitions, i.e. module, group, function, altstep, test case, control, and component type definitions can have an optional attribute.

requirements.original: When an optional attribute is associated to a function, altstep, test case, control or component type definitions, it shall have effect on all the constants, module parameters, templates, variables and template variables declared within these definitions and not on the enframing definition itself.
requirements.canonical: When an optional attribute is associated with a function, altstep, testcase, module control function or component type definition, it SHALL have effect on all constants, module parameters, templates, variables and template variables declared within that definition.
requirements.condition: optional attribute associated with a function, altstep, testcase, control or component type definition
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.7 -- When an optional attribute is associated to a function, altstep, test case, control or component type definitions, it shall have effect on all the constants, module parameters, templates, variables and template variables declared within these definitions and not on the enframing definition itself.

requirements.original: When no value of the optional attribute is explicitly specified for a definition (either directly or inherited from the surrounding scope), the value of the optional attribute is implicitly set to "explicit omit" for that definition.
requirements.canonical: When no value of the optional attribute is specified for a definition, either directly or inherited from the surrounding scope, the optional attribute of that definition IS implicitly "explicit omit".
requirements.condition: no optional attribute value specified directly or inherited
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.7 -- When no value of the optional attribute is explicitly specified for a definition (either directly or inherited from the surrounding scope), the value of the optional attribute is implicitly set to "explicit omit" for that definition.

requirements.original: a) "implicit omit" means that all optional fields, that have no assigned value definition in the statement on which the attribute operates, are set to omit.
requirements.canonical: With the optional attribute "implicit omit", every optional field that has no assigned value definition in the statement on which the attribute operates IS set to `omit`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.7 -- a) "implicit omit" means that all optional fields, that have no assigned value definition in the statement on which the attribute operates, are set to omit.

requirements.original: This applies recursively to the optional fields of the entity and to subfields of the mandatory fields.
requirements.canonical: The "implicit omit" rule IS applied recursively to the optional fields of the entity and to the subfields of its mandatory fields.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.7 -- This applies recursively to the optional fields of the entity and to subfields of the mandatory fields.

requirements.original: b) "explicit omit" means that all optional fields, that have no assigned value definition in the statement on which the attribute operates, are left undefined.
requirements.canonical: With the optional attribute "explicit omit", every optional field that has no assigned value definition in the statement on which the attribute operates IS left undefined.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.7 -- b) "explicit omit" means that all optional fields, that have no assigned value definition in the statement on which the attribute operates, are left undefined.

requirements.original: This applies recursively to the optional fields of the entity and to subfields of the mandatory fields.
requirements.canonical: The "explicit omit" rule IS applied recursively to the optional fields of the entity and to the subfields of its mandatory fields.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.7 -- This applies recursively to the optional fields of the entity and to subfields of the mandatory fields.

requirements.original: For variables and template variables associated with an "implicit omit" optional attribute, recursive procedure is applied to their optional fields after each assignment or usage as out or inout actual parameter in the scope of their declaration (e.g. after re-assigning parts or all of a variable's value) setting all optional fields that have no assigned value definition to omit.
requirements.canonical: For a variable or template variable associated with an "implicit omit" optional attribute, the recursive procedure SHALL be applied after each assignment in the scope of its declaration, setting all optional fields without an assigned value definition to `omit`.
requirements.condition: variable or template variable with "implicit omit"
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.7 -- For variables and template variables associated with an "implicit omit" optional attribute, recursive procedure is applied to their optional fields after each assignment or usage as out or inout actual parameter in the scope of their declaration (e.g. after re-assigning parts or all of a variable's value) setting all optional fields that have no assigned value definition to omit.

requirements.original: For variables and template variables associated with an "implicit omit" optional attribute, recursive procedure is applied to their optional fields after each assignment or usage as out or inout actual parameter in the scope of their declaration (e.g. after re-assigning parts or all of a variable's value) setting all optional fields that have no assigned value definition to omit.
requirements.canonical: For a variable or template variable associated with an "implicit omit" optional attribute, the recursive procedure SHALL be applied after each usage of it as an `out` or `inout` actual parameter in the scope of its declaration, setting all optional fields without an assigned value definition to `omit`.
requirements.condition: variable or template variable with "implicit omit" used as out or inout actual parameter
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.7 -- For variables and template variables associated with an "implicit omit" optional attribute, recursive procedure is applied to their optional fields after each assignment or usage as out or inout actual parameter in the scope of their declaration (e.g. after re-assigning parts or all of a variable's value) setting all optional fields that have no assigned value definition to omit.

requirements.original: a) Data type, port type, procedure signature and import statements shall not have an optional attribute associated to them directly.
requirements.canonical: An optional attribute SHALL NOT be associated directly with a data type definition, port type definition, procedure signature definition or import statement.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.7 -- a) Data type, port type, procedure signature and import statements shall not have an optional attribute associated to them directly.

requirements.original: b) At most one optional attribute shall be applied to each definition, each individual field reference or language element to which a with statement is associated.
requirements.canonical: At most one optional attribute SHALL be applied to each definition, each individual field reference or language element to which a with statement is associated.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.7 -- b) At most one optional attribute shall be applied to each definition, each individual field reference or language element to which a with statement is associated.

requirements.original: TTCN-3 provides a set of operations that can be used for retrieving attribute values associated with a type, template, variable, constant or module parameter.
requirements.canonical: TTCN-3 provides operations for retrieving the attribute values associated with a type, template, variable, constant or module parameter.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.8 -- TTCN-3 provides a set of operations that can be used for retrieving attribute values associated with a type, template, variable, constant or module parameter.

requirements.original: ( Type | TemplateInstance ) "." ( display | encode | variant | extension | optional ) [ "(" Expression ")" ]
requirements.canonical: An attribute retrieval operation has the syntax ( Type | TemplateInstance ) "." ( `display` | `encode` | `variant` | `extension` | `optional` ) [ "(" Expression ")" ].
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.8 -- ( Type | TemplateInstance ) "." ( display | encode | variant | extension | optional ) [ "(" Expression ")" ]

requirements.original: The operation returns the actual value of an attribute associated with the type, template, variable, constant or module parameter that precedes the dot symbol.
requirements.canonical: An attribute retrieval operation returns the actual value of the attribute associated with the type, template, variable, constant or module parameter preceding the dot.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.8 -- The operation returns the actual value of an attribute associated with the type, template, variable, constant or module parameter that precedes the dot symbol.

requirements.original: The value preceding the dot symbol may be unitialized.
requirements.canonical: The variable or template preceding the dot of an attribute retrieval operation MAY be uninitialized.

ambiguity.issue: "value" is used for the entity preceding the dot, which is a type or template instance; "unitialized" is a misspelling of the glossary term "uninitialized".

improper_terms.proper: variable, constant, template or module parameter (TemplateInstance)

requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.8 -- The value preceding the dot symbol may be unitialized.

requirements.original: The attribute kind is denoted by the keyword following the dot symbol.
requirements.canonical: The attribute kind retrieved by an attribute retrieval operation IS denoted by the keyword (`display`, `encode`, `variant`, `extension` or `optional`) following the dot.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.8 -- The attribute kind is denoted by the keyword following the dot symbol.

requirements.original: The return value of the operations for retrieving attribute values is of a universal charstring type in case of attributes that can be present only once (display, optional) .
requirements.canonical: An attribute retrieval operation for an attribute that can be present only once (`display`, `optional`) returns a value of universal charstring type.
requirements.condition: display or optional attribute
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.8 -- The return value of the operations for retrieving attribute values is of a universal charstring type in case of attributes that can be present only once (display, optional) .

requirements.original: If such an attribute is not defined, the operation returns an empty string.
requirements.canonical: If a `display` or `optional` attribute is not defined, the attribute retrieval operation returns an empty string.
requirements.condition: display or optional attribute not defined
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.8 -- If such an attribute is not defined, the operation returns an empty string.

requirements.original: If the attribute can occur multiple times (encode, variant, extension), the operation returns a record of universal charstring type.
requirements.canonical: An attribute retrieval operation for an attribute that can occur multiple times (`encode`, `variant`, `extension`) returns a value of a record of universal charstring type.
requirements.condition: encode, variant or extension attribute

ambiguity.issue: It is not stated which "record of universal charstring" type is returned (no predefined type exists); the example assigns it to a user-defined type RUC. Chose: a value compatible with any record of universal charstring type.
readings: An attribute retrieval operation for `encode`, `variant` or `extension` returns a value compatible with any record of universal charstring type.
An attribute retrieval operation for `encode`, `variant` or `extension` returns a value of one specific (implicitly predefined) record of universal charstring type.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.8 -- If the attribute can occur multiple times (encode, variant, extension), the operation returns a record of universal charstring type.

requirements.original: If such an attribute is not present, the operation returns an empty record of value.
requirements.canonical: If an `encode`, `variant` or `extension` attribute is not present, the attribute retrieval operation returns an empty record of value.
requirements.condition: encode, variant or extension attribute not present
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.8 -- If such an attribute is not present, the operation returns an empty record of value.

requirements.original: The operation for getting a variant attribute value may be followed by an optional parameter.
requirements.canonical: An attribute retrieval operation for a `variant` attribute MAY be followed by an optional parameter.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.8 -- The operation for getting a variant attribute value may be followed by an optional parameter.

requirements.original: If no parameter is present, the operation returns only variants that are not bound to any particular encoding.
requirements.canonical: If no parameter is present, the `variant` attribute retrieval operation returns only the variants that are not bound to any particular encoding.
requirements.condition: no parameter
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.8 -- If no parameter is present, the operation returns only variants that are not bound to any particular encoding.

requirements.original: If the parameter is present, the returned value will contain variants that are bound to the encoding referenced by the parameter.
requirements.canonical: If the parameter is present, the `variant` attribute retrieval operation returns the variants that are bound to the encoding referenced by the parameter.
requirements.condition: parameter present

ambiguity.issue: "will contain variants that are bound to the encoding" does not say whether variants not bound to any encoding are also included. Chose: only the bound variants.
readings: If the parameter is present, the `variant` attribute retrieval operation returns only the variants bound to the referenced encoding.
If the parameter is present, the `variant` attribute retrieval operation returns the variants bound to the referenced encoding plus the variants not bound to any encoding.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.8 -- If the parameter is present, the returned value will contain variants that are bound to the encoding referenced by the parameter.

requirements.original: a) The optional parameter of the operation shall be used only for getting variant attributes.
requirements.canonical: The optional parameter of an attribute retrieval operation SHALL be used only for retrieving `variant` attributes.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.8 -- a) The optional parameter of the operation shall be used only for getting variant attributes.

requirements.original: b) The Expression in optional parameter of the operation shall be of the universal charstring type.
requirements.canonical: The Expression in the optional parameter of an attribute retrieval operation SHALL be of universal charstring type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.8 -- b) The Expression in optional parameter of the operation shall be of the universal charstring type.

requirements.original: c) An error shall be produced if the Expression in the optional parameters is not one of the valid encode attributes.
requirements.canonical: An error SHALL be produced if the Expression in the optional parameter of an attribute retrieval operation is not one of the valid encode attributes of the referenced type or template.
requirements.condition: parameter value is not a valid encode attribute

ambiguity.issue: It is not stated whether the error is a compile-time error (when the Expression is constant) or a runtime error, nor whose encode attributes are meant. Chose: the encode attributes of the entity preceding the dot, checked whenever the value is known.
readings: A compile-time error SHALL be produced if the constant Expression is not one of the encode attributes of the entity preceding the dot.
A runtime error SHALL be produced when the evaluated Expression is not one of the encode attributes of the entity preceding the dot.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.8 -- c) An error shall be produced if the Expression in the optional parameters is not one of the valid encode attributes.

requirements.original: The setencode operation can be used on a port or set of ports to dynamically select for the affected ports a single encode attribute value to be used for a type that has multiple encode attributes attached to it.
requirements.canonical: The `setencode` operation CAN be used on a port or set of ports to dynamically select, for the affected ports, a single encode attribute value for a type that has multiple encode attributes.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.9 -- The setencode operation can be used on a port or set of ports to dynamically select for the affected ports a single encode attribute value to be used for a type that has multiple encode attributes attached to it.

requirements.original: (SingleExpression | ( all port ) | self ) "." setencode"(" Type "," SingleExpression ")"
requirements.canonical: The `setencode` operation has the syntax ( SingleExpression | `all port` | `self` ) "." `setencode` "(" Type "," SingleExpression ")".
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.9 -- (SingleExpression | ( all port ) | self ) "." setencode"(" Type "," SingleExpression ")"

requirements.original: The setencode operation dynamically restricts the number of encode attribute values of a referenced type or its fields or elements to a single value.
requirements.canonical: The `setencode` operation dynamically restricts the encode attribute values of the referenced type, or of its fields or elements, to a single value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.9 -- The setencode operation dynamically restricts the number of encode attribute values of a referenced type or its fields or elements to a single value.

requirements.original: Dependent on the language element preceding the dot, the encoding configuration is valid either for all sending and receiving operations of a single port (single port reference), sending and receiving operations of all ports of the current component (all `port notation) or for all codec functions and communication operations of` the current component (self keyword).
requirements.canonical: When the `setencode` operation is applied to a single port reference, the encoding configuration IS valid for all sending and receiving operations of that port.
requirements.condition: single port reference precedes the dot
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.9 -- Dependent on the language element preceding the dot, the encoding configuration is valid either for all sending and receiving operations of a single port (single port reference), sending and receiving operations of all ports of the current component (all `port notation) or for all codec functions and communication operations of` the current component (self keyword).

requirements.original: Dependent on the language element preceding the dot, the encoding configuration is valid either for all sending and receiving operations of a single port (single port reference), sending and receiving operations of all ports of the current component (all `port notation) or for all codec functions and communication operations of` the current component (self keyword).
requirements.canonical: When the `setencode` operation is applied with `all port`, the encoding configuration IS valid for the sending and receiving operations of all ports of the current component.
requirements.condition: `all port` precedes the dot
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.9 -- Dependent on the language element preceding the dot, the encoding configuration is valid either for all sending and receiving operations of a single port (single port reference), sending and receiving operations of all ports of the current component (all `port notation) or for all codec functions and communication operations of` the current component (self keyword).

requirements.original: Dependent on the language element preceding the dot, the encoding configuration is valid either for all sending and receiving operations of a single port (single port reference), sending and receiving operations of all ports of the current component (all `port notation) or for all codec functions and communication operations of` the current component (self keyword).
requirements.canonical: When the `setencode` operation is applied with `self`, the encoding configuration IS valid for all codec functions and communication operations of the current component.
requirements.condition: `self` precedes the dot
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.9 -- Dependent on the language element preceding the dot, the encoding configuration is valid either for all sending and receiving operations of a single port (single port reference), sending and receiving operations of all ports of the current component (all `port notation) or for all codec functions and communication operations of` the current component (self keyword).

requirements.original: If the referenced type contains multiple encode attributes and the expression provided in the setencode operation is equal to one of these encode attribute values, the statement reduces the list of encode attributes to the selected one.
requirements.canonical: If the referenced type contains multiple encode attributes and the expression of the `setencode` operation equals one of them, the `setencode` operation reduces the list of encode attributes to the selected one.
requirements.condition: type has multiple encode attributes and expression equals one of them

ambiguity.issue: The behaviour when the expression matches none of the encode attributes (or the type has only one) is not specified. Chose: the stated case only.
readings: If the expression matches none of the encode attributes, the `setencode` operation has no effect.
If the expression matches none of the encode attributes, the `setencode` operation causes an error.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.9 -- If the referenced type contains multiple encode attributes and the expression provided in the setencode operation is equal to one of these encode attribute values, the statement reduces the list of encode attributes to the selected one.

requirements.original: The procedure is applied recursively to all elements and fields or the referenced type.
requirements.canonical: The `setencode` reduction procedure IS applied recursively to all elements and fields of the referenced type.

ambiguity.issue: "fields or the referenced type" is a typo for "fields of the referenced type".

requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.9 -- The procedure is applied recursively to all elements and fields or the referenced type.

requirements.original: After executing the operation, all other encode attributes and variants related to them are dynamically disabled and invisible to the codec.
requirements.canonical: After the `setencode` operation is executed, all other encode attributes of the referenced type and the variants related to them IS dynamically disabled and invisible to the codec.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.9 -- After executing the operation, all other encode attributes and variants related to them are dynamically disabled and invisible to the codec.

requirements.original: Repeated call of the setencode operation always uses the static attributes that are valid for the referenced type.
requirements.canonical: A repeated call of the `setencode` operation always uses the static attributes that are valid for the referenced type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.9 -- Repeated call of the setencode operation always uses the static attributes that are valid for the referenced type.

requirements.original: Previous calls of the setencode operation referencing the type are not considered in this case.
requirements.canonical: Previous calls of the `setencode` operation referencing the same type IS NOT considered by a repeated call.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.9 -- Previous calls of the setencode operation referencing the type are not considered in this case.

requirements.original: This way it is possible to change the encoding during test execution using different encodings.
requirements.canonical: The encoding of a type CAN be changed during test execution by repeated `setencode` calls using different encodings.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.9 -- This way it is possible to change the encoding during test execution using different encodings.

requirements.original: It is allowed to reference a field or element of a type using an extended type reference in the setencode operation.
requirements.canonical: The `setencode` operation MAY reference a field or element of a type using an extended type reference.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.9 -- It is allowed to reference a field or element of a type using an extended type reference in the setencode operation.

requirements.original: If the extended type reference is used, following calls of the setencode operation for the whole type or any element that contains the referenced payload field won't change the encoding that was dynamically configured for this field or element (and its sub-fields).
requirements.canonical: If an extended type reference was used in a `setencode` operation, subsequent `setencode` calls for the whole type or any element containing the referenced field SHALL NOT change the encoding dynamically configured for that field or element and its sub-fields.
requirements.condition: an extended type reference was used in an earlier setencode call
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.9 -- If the extended type reference is used, following calls of the setencode operation for the whole type or any element that contains the referenced payload field won't change the encoding that was dynamically configured for this field or element (and its sub-fields).

requirements.original: a) If the setencode operation is applied to a single port, the referenced type shall be either listed in the in or out type list of the related port type or it shall be a reference to a field or element on any level of nesting of a type listed in the in or out type list of the related port type.
requirements.canonical: If the `setencode` operation is applied to a single port, the referenced type SHALL be listed in the in or out type list of the related port type, or be a reference to a field or element, on any level of nesting, of such a type.
requirements.condition: setencode applied to a single port

ambiguity.issue: The port type lists are "in", "out" and "inout"; the restriction mentions only "in or out". The example uses an inout list. Chose: types in in, out or inout lists are allowed.
readings: If `setencode` is applied to a single port, the referenced type SHALL be listed in the in, out or inout list of the port type (or be a nested field of such a type).
If `setencode` is applied to a single port, the referenced type SHALL be listed in the in or out list of the port type only (or be a nested field of such a type).

requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.9 -- a) If the setencode operation is applied to a single port, the referenced type shall be either listed in the in or out type list of the related port type or it shall be a reference to a field or element on any level of nesting of a type listed in the in or out type list of the related port type.

requirements.original: b) The SingleExpression used in the second parameter of the setencode operation shall be compatible with the universal charstring type.
requirements.canonical: The SingleExpression in the second parameter of the `setencode` operation SHALL be compatible with the universal charstring type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.9 -- b) The SingleExpression used in the second parameter of the setencode operation shall be compatible with the universal charstring type.

requirements.original: c) If present, the SingleExpression preceding the setencode keyword shall be of a port type.
requirements.canonical: If present, the SingleExpression preceding the `setencode` keyword SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.condition: a SingleExpression precedes the dot
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.9 -- c) If present, the SingleExpression preceding the setencode keyword shall be of a port type.
